description:
Allow a kernel to be written as Elixir writes multi-clause functions: one bodiless typed head (`defk dod_bits(acc :: bitstring, dod :: i64) :: bitstring`), then clauses whose parameters use the patterns `case` already supports (integer/bool literals, variables, `_`) with optional guards. Compiles to a `case` over the parameters (no cost over the hand `cond`); no clause matching raises FunctionClauseError, as in Elixir. Applies to entry and helper kernels. Needed by Gorilla's delta-of-delta bucket choice (gorilla_stream encoder/delta_encoding.ex).

Each accepted convenience construct needs: an Elixir-mode meaning, agreement tests (Defk.Case, both modes), and a docs/language.md entry. Decided in 'Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?' (defk-dtw.18); sketches on branch prototype/defk-dtw.18-sketches (prototypes/convenience_sketches.exs).

Done when the Gorilla dod_bits shape compiles, both modes agree including FunctionClauseError, and a clause without a head (or with types in a non-head clause) gets an actionable compile error.

comments.text: Decisions: (1) Defk.Clauses.merge/1 runs in Defk.__before_compile__ (after attribute inlining) and turns a bodiless head plus its clauses into one kernel whose body is a case, so the compiler and Elixir mode need no new construct. Subject = the first parameter some clause matches with a literal (else the literal true); literals at other parameters become param === lit tests ANDed in front of the guard (Elixir matches before guarding, and 'and' short-circuits, so a guard error still fails the clause). (2) No copies: clause variables are renamed to the head parameter at their position in guard and body; head names a clause does not bind are renamed to a hidden name, so an unbound use is undefined-variable (reported under the user's name via meta defk_name) and a body may still bind them as fresh locals. (3) The case carries meta defk_clauses: {name, arity}; its no-match path raises %FunctionClauseError{module, function, arity} with kind/args/clauses nil (exactly what Elixir raises, checked field for field against plain defs). Natively a new runtime kind DEFK_E_FUN_CLAUSE with a static 'Elixir.Mod\0name' string; for an inlined helper function is the helper, as for a defp. (4) Patterns: i64 literals, bool literals, variables, _; ^pin (Elixir rejects it in heads too), floats, tuples, repeated variables and wrong-typed literals are clause-pattern. Errors: clause-head (no head, or a clause before it; hint names the params after the clause variables), clause-types (types or return type on a clause), unknown-option (options on a clause), no-body (head without clauses), duplicate-kernel (two heads; now kind :error, not :planned). (5) Generated C: identical to the hand cond apart from the case's own subject local (test compares normalised C); literal dispatch is an if-chain. (6) Side fixes: generated argument variables drop a leading underscore (a _name parameter warned 'underscored variable used' in the dispatch def and __defk_elixir__ before this), and keyword options written with do: (defk f(...) :: t, yield: false, do: x) are no longer dropped. Doc example checker substitutes the alias for the module name in raise messages so FunctionClauseError can be documented. Tests: test/multi_clause_test.exs.

title: Multi-clause kernels with a typed function head
